evidence.note: Dependency-aware foundation-first order: verify vendored-lib hashes and install deps, then build storage (database.py) with compile-checks before any endpoints or UI — de-risks foundations everything else depends on.

Restructured into config/utils → routes_oauth (auth) → routes_api → routes_ui → main assembly → templates → static, a defensible layered build order; each file compile-verified as a per-item done-check.

Testing pass used explicit done-criteria tied to the spec's thresholds (seed counts ≥8/≥20/≥3/≥2, palette #563acc, CSP, cookie flags, OAuth end-to-end) — real verification hooks rather than 'it starts'.
Back half collapsed into ~60 near-identical 'close the heredoc' plans with no milestone progress and no re-scoping; planning became repetitive ceremony, not a revised, living hierarchy.

reasoning: The agent built a defensibly dependency-aware sequence (hashes+deps → storage → auth → API → UI → static → seed-verification) and attached genuine done-checks (compile checks, seed-count thresholds, palette/CSP/cookie/OAuth verification), which is clearly above the 'sensible ordered plan' anchor (5). It falls short of 8 because the milestones were never expressed as an explicit hierarchy with declared verification hooks up front — they were rolling re-plans, and the criteria emerged in practice — and the long degenerate loop in the back half shows none of the revised, self-correcting milestone re-scoping the higher anchors describe. That places it at a 6.
